# National Development Parallel Coordinates Dataset

## Overview
This dataset contains 30 countries spanning four World Bank income groups (High, Upper-Middle, Lower-Middle, Low) with seven development indicators, designed for a parallel coordinates visualization of multidimensional national profiles.

## Data Source

### national_development
Each record represents one country with the following fields:
- **country** (string): Country name
- **income_group** (string): World Bank income classification — one of High, Upper-Middle, Lower-Middle, Low
- **gdp_per_capita_usd** (numeric): GDP per capita in current USD, range ~380–87,720
- **hdi** (numeric): Human Development Index, range 0.394–0.961
- **freedom_index** (numeric): Freedom House aggregate score, 0–100 (100 = most free)
- **corruption_perceptions_index** (numeric): Transparency International CPI score, 0–100 (100 = least corrupt)
- **co2_emissions_per_capita_tons** (numeric): Annual CO₂ emissions in metric tons per capita, range 0.1–21.8
- **military_expenditure_pct_gdp** (numeric): Military spending as percentage of GDP, range 0.6–6.0
- **internet_penetration_pct** (numeric): Percentage of population using the internet, range 14–99

## Data Notes
- Values are approximate 2023 estimates compiled from World Bank, UNDP, Freedom House, Transparency International, IEA, SIPRI, and ITU.
- Income group assignments follow the World Bank July 2023 classification.
- Some values for conflict-affected states (e.g., Afghanistan) carry higher uncertainty.
- CO₂ figures are production-based and exclude land-use change emissions.

Skip to content
Global Development Analysis · 2023

National Development Profiles

Parallel coordinates across 7 dimensions for 30 countries, colored by World Bank income group. Each line represents one country's profile — follow how lines converge, diverge, and cross between axes to reveal structural patterns in global development.

Income Group
Click to filter · Hover lines for detail
Seven Dimensions of National Development
GDP per Capita · HDI · Freedom Index · Corruption Perceptions · CO₂ per Capita · Military % GDP · Internet Penetration — each axis independently scaled

Income Group Separation

High-income nations cluster near the top of GDP, HDI, and Internet axes. The clearest divergence from low-income nations occurs on GDP per capita (up to 230× difference) and Internet penetration, where lines rarely overlap.

Freedom–Corruption Cluster

Freedom Index and Corruption Perceptions Index lines move largely in parallel for most countries — high freedom correlates with low corruption. Notable exception: Singapore scores very high on CPI (83) yet only moderately on Freedom (47).

Nonlinear Crossovers

GDP → HDI shows significant compression: Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Singapore have high GDP but HDI lower than European peers, reflecting wealth-welfare gaps. Freedom → Corruption axes show sharp crossovers for authoritarian-but-wealthy states.

High-Income Outliers

Saudi Arabia (Freedom: 7) and UAE (Freedom: 17) stand out among high-income nations with very low freedom scores, creating sharp downward crossings on the Freedom axis compared to Western peers. Both also have extremely high CO₂ emissions (18–22 tons per capita).

CO₂ Paradox

High CO₂ emitters span all income groups unexpectedly. The US and Australia (high-income) emit 14–15 tons/capita, while UAE and Saudi Arabia emit 18–22 tons, yet lower-middle income Vietnam and India emit only 1.9–3.5 tons — income does not linearly determine carbon footprint.

Upper-Middle Divergence

Upper-middle income nations show the widest variance, particularly in Freedom (China: 9 vs. Brazil: 73) and CO₂ emissions (Colombia: 1.8 vs. Russia: 11.4). This group contains both democratic and authoritarian states, unlike high-income nations which cluster toward freedom.

Notable Outlier Profiles

Countries whose profiles deviate most dramatically from their income-group peers
